title: Platform systems & services operational playbook — dashboards, runbooks, and roadmap
author: Daniel Kim
summary: Operational playbook for Platform Engineering covering service inventory, dashboards and alerting standards, runbooks for high-severity incidents, retrospective cadence and a near-term roadmap for systems and services.
body:
Overview

This document is the canonical playbook for the Platform team’s systems and services. It covers: a concise service inventory, dashboard and alerting standards, runbooks for common incident patterns, retrospective and postmortem cadence, and the near-term roadmap (Q1–Q3 2026). Owners, SLAs, and escalation paths are explicit to enable fast, consistent response.

1) Systems & Services inventory (high level)
- control-plane-api: fronting internal Console and API traffic. Owner: platform-control-plane team. SLO: 99.95% p99 latency <= 150ms. Critical alerts: error_rate > 0.5% for 5m, p95 latency > 300ms for 5m.
- routing-service: smart request router for model variant selection. Owner: routing team. SLO: 99.9% availability. Critical alerts: 5xx rate > 0.2% for 10m, outlier host count >= 3.
- batch-cache: prefix & KV cache layer used by serving runtime. Owner: runtime-caching team. SLO: cache-hit >= 70% for high-throughput workloads. Critical alerts: cache eviction rate spike > 200% baseline.
- monitoring & metrics pipeline: Prometheus + Cortex + Grafana. Owner: observability team. SLO: metrics ingest latency < 60s. Critical alerts: backend write errors > 1% for 10m.

2) Dashboards and alerting standards
- Naming conventions: Product-Component-View (e.g., Platform-Control-Plane-Overview). Use consistent tags: team:, service:, severity:.
- Dashboard types:
  - SLO Overview: per-service SLI charts (availability, latency, error_rate).
  - Capacity & Resource: GPU utilization, node counts, queue lengths.
  - Health: rolling 5m/1h error rates, request volumes, cache hit ratios.
  - Cost: token consumption per model, billing estimates per pool.
- Alerting policy (standard):
  1. SEV0 (P1): Service down, customer-impacting (e.g., control-plane 5xx > 2% for 5m). PagerDuty: platform oncall, paging rule immediate.
  2. SEV1 (P2): Degraded but operational (e.g., p99 latency > SLO for 30m). Slack and email to owners, oncall paged if persists > 60m.
  3. SEV2 (P3): Operational issue with low customer impact (e.g., cache-hit drop < 50% for 60m). Create incident ticket, notify owners.
- Alert content template (must include): title, impacted service, metric & threshold, time window, observed value, runbook link, primary owner, escalation contact.

3) Example dashboard table
| Dashboard | Purpose | Owner | Key widgets | Runbook |
| Platform-Control-Plane-Overview | High-level health for control plane | platform-control-plane | availability, p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, request volume | control-plane-runbook |
| Routing-Service-Health | Router performance & fallbacks | routing | route success rate, fallback count, host health | routing-runbook |

4) Runbooks (templates and key runbooks)
- Runbook template (shared):
  - Title
  - Symptoms (what users/operators observe)
  - Incident severity mapping
  - Immediate mitigation steps (commands, toggles)
  - Diagnostic checklist (logs, traces, metric queries)
  - Rollback criteria & steps
  - Postmortem owner and timeline

- control-plane-runbook (summary):
  1. Verify alert: check Grafana SLO dashboard and PagerDuty alert notes.
  2. Mitigate (fast path): scale control-plane deployment by +25% (kubectl/helm commands), enable read-only mode for console (feature flag), route traffic away from degraded region.
  3. Investigate: collect logs (kubectl logs, Loki), trace path (Jaeger) for top 10 failing request ids, check DB connection pool metrics.
  4. Escalation: if error_rate stays > 1% after mitigations +15m, page SRE tech lead and database owner.
  5. Post-incident: open postmortem within 24h, assign owner for RCA and follow-ups.

- routing-runbook (summary):
  1. Confirm degraded decisions: check routing-service fallbacks, compare model variant availability.
  2. Toggle fallback thresholds to reduce churn (config: routing/fallbacks/{percent}).
  3. Check KV cache and connectivity to model pools; flush prefix cache for affected routes if corruption suspected.

5) Retrospective & postmortem process
- Triage window: Initial incident triage within 2 hours, postmortem created within 24 hours for SEV0/SEV1.
- Template requirements: timeline, impact statement (customers affected), root cause, corrective actions (owner + due date), metrics showing remediation.
- Quarterly reliability retro: collate top incidents and trend charts to set reliability OKRs. Retrospectives are shared at the Platform All-Hands.

6) On-call & escalation matrix
- Primary oncall: platform oncall rotation (2-week rotations). Secondary oncall: platform-sre. PagerDuty playbooks must include Slack channel, phone escalation list, and exec notify policy for SEV0.
- Contact list (owners): platform-control-plane (control-plane-owner@redwood.ai), routing (routing-owner@redwood.ai), observability (obs-owner@redwood.ai).

7) Roadmap (near-term priorities, Q1–Q3 2026)
- Q1 2026: Migrate metrics backend to Cortex 2.0 for reduced ingest latency; standardize dashboard templates and ship dashboard-as-code repo.
- Q2 2026: Implement adaptive alerting (machine-learned baselines) for lower false positives; rollout unified runbook templates in Confluence with runbook links in alerts.
- Q3 2026: Service-level auto-remediation experiments (safe, opt-in): automated cache warming and controlled rollback for model variants.

8) How-tos and quick references
- Add a new dashboard: copy Dashboard Template > update tags (team:, service:, severity:) > link to runbook > request review from observability team.
- Create an alert: use Alert Wizard > include alert content template fields > set SLO-based suppression for known maintenance windows.
- Emergency scale: kubectl -n platform scale deployment control-plane --replicas=$(($(kubectl get deploy control-plane -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}') + 3))

9) Ownership & governance
- Owners must keep runbooks and dashboards up-to-date. Oncall handover checklist includes reviewing open runbooks and dashboard alerts. Observability team performs monthly alert reviews and triage to reduce noise.

Appendix: Links and templates
- Runbook template: /confluence/eng-platform/runbook-template
- Dashboard template: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboard-template
- PagerDuty playbooks: /confluence/eng-platform/pagerduty-playbooks

If you are an owner of a service listed here and need an update or want to adopt a different SLO, file a request in the Platform backlog and assign to the observability lead for review.
